providers/Soundcloud/soundcloud_media_in:
The retry loop never terminates

retry is initialised to 0 and never incremented, so while retry < retrys only ends through the break that requires medialist to be non-empty. If the browser finds nothing, this loops forever and starts a visible Chromium on every pass. The TaskFailedError below the loop is unreachable in that case.

YouTube Music had the same loop and has been fixed by incrementing the counter; the same line is missing here.

The two older problems in this provider are gone: actions is a list of dicts now, so both clicks run, and the download type is no longer pinned to HLS — makeProviderResult() decides it.
providers/Youtube/Youtube.py:
Not imported

This is the pre-split monolith. Youtube/__init__.py re-exports from youtube_search.py, youtube_media_information.py and music_youtube_*.py instead, so nothing here runs. Kept for reference; do not read it as current behaviour.
providers/Soundcloud/Soundcloud.py:
Not imported

The pre-split file. Soundcloud/__init__.py pulls from the three smaller modules instead.
providers/models.py:
Complete candidates start at −1

The base score is only computed for candidates without an extension. A candidate that arrives complete keeps prio = -1, and the winner has to beat the initial −1 — so without a matching preferred_file or preferred_type it is never picked and the call ends in „Didn't find any media“.

Separately, MEDIA_EXTENSION_PRIORITY mixes containers (mp4, mp3) with playlist formats (m3u8, mpd), so a +1000 for preferred_file lets a progressive URL outrank a playlist even where HLS was intended.
core/models/Download.py:
Two methods read fields that do not exist

DownloadTarget.__str__ reads self.job_id and self.out_file; the dataclass has neither. Any print(target) ends in an AttributeError. The same applies to DownloadInformation.toDict(), which uses self.context_id instead of self.job_id.
core/download/Dispatcher/base.py:
The error check sits one level too deep

In downloadToFile() the if resultList: raise ... is inside the for loop over the results. As soon as one error is collected the loop aborts — later results are never checked and never appear in the combined message.
core/network/Session.py:
The cookie path depends on the working directory

ROOT_DIR = os.getcwd() is evaluated at import time. If the server starts from a different directory, COOKIE_FILE points somewhere else and logins appear lost even though the file exists. Soundcloud/soundcloud_browser.py repeats the same pattern locally.
providers/Youtube/youtube_media_informat:
The fallbacks never run

_extractSeperatedVideoAudioFromFormats() checks if not bestVideoCandidate, but a BestCandidate instance is always truthy. The function always returns a result — with an empty URL if no format had one — so the hlsManifestUrl and progressive-format branches in _tryGetUsableUrls() are unreachable. Test .url instead.

Also: every call writes youtube_formats.txt into the working directory, and _sendRequest() stores X-Goog-Visitor-Id in the shared header dictionary from youtube_models, so it leaks into later requests.
providers/Filmpalast/filmpalast_media_in:
Work in progress

The function decodes the host links and opens a visible browser for each, but has no return: it hands back None instead of a ProviderResult. The provider is registered in both mappings, so a download request for it gets as far as building the context and fails there.
core/download/UMP/dispatcher.py:
SABR streaming sends nothing

In _runContextStream() the sabr branch creates generator and never iterates it; the context is marked FINISHED with zero bytes. In _runContextLocal() the UMP branch writes TaskStatus.FINISHED into download_progress.speed instead of status.
core/download/HLS/dispatcher.py:
The local path predates the rework

_runContextLocal() still passes a context to MasterHLSDownload and IndexHLSDownload, which now take URLs, and calls downloadToFile() without its out_file and download_progress arguments. Only _runContextStream() is current; the server has LOCAL downloads switched off.
core/network/file.py:
Ranged downloads need a size

asyncDownloadYieldRanges() loops while start < total_size. With the −1 that getUrlInformation() returns for an unknown size, it yields nothing and ends without an error.
core/ffmpeg/ffmpeg_download.py:
Not used by the dispatchers

FFmpegDownload lets ffmpeg fetch the URLs itself. It is exported from core.ffmpeg, but the download path uses AsyncFFmpegMuxer fed from the engine's own downloaders instead.
